message:
Choose the feature to start from this roadmap inventory. Dependency arrows mean depends on; direct unlocks and downstream dependents are different measures.
The configured roadmap is .specify/memory/roadmap.md. Planned entries require every prerequisite to be verified. Verified, deferred, abandoned, already-active, and ambiguous entries are excluded.

| Choice | Exact entry ID/title | Status | Prerequisites | direct_unlock_count | downstream_dependent_count |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 804 — Count Lines | planned | 801 — Text Foundation (verified) | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | defer | — | — | — | — |

802 — Normalize Text is dependency-ready through verified 801, but is unsafe as a new-start candidate: both 802 and verified 801 map to existing specs/801-text-foundation/, whose specification is Text Foundation. The active pointer also identifies this directory. The competing mapping makes ownership and active identity ambiguous; 802 is excluded rather than treated as selectable. 801 is terminal and excluded.

803 — Batch Normalization (planned) is blocked because its prerequisite 802 — Normalize Text remains planned and additionally has an ambiguous mapping. Completing 802 under valid authority would directly unlock 803 (one direct unlock and one unfinished transitive dependent), but that hypothetical impact does not make 802 safe to select.

Full prerequisite closures (arrow means depends on):
803 — Batch Normalization [planned] -> 802 — Normalize Text [planned; mapping conflict] -> 801 — Text Foundation [verified]
802 — Normalize Text [planned; mapping conflict] -> 801 — Text Foundation [verified]
804 — Count Lines [planned] -> 801 — Text Foundation [verified]
There are no missing dependency references or cycles. Only 804 is safely selectable; no choice has been made.

Required authority question for the requested 802 direction: Which roadmap entry owns specs/801-text-foundation/, and what exact approved Spec dir mapping should 802 — Normalize Text use before activation? Resolve the competing 801/802 mapping through an explicit approved patch, then reassess availability. No conflict repair, pointer substitution, specification creation, or roadmap change was performed.
We can discuss dependency chains and which prerequisites unblock the most work before you choose. Keep this gate pending while answering those questions from the inventory; a question is not a selection. Select one exact listed entry or defer. Choosing a feature does not approve a roadmap patch.
